newsitem.title: FINLAND: METSA-SERLA TO SELLS ITS CHEMICALS PLANTS.
newsitem.headline: METSA-SERLA TO SELLS ITS CHEMICALS PLANTS.

text.p: Finnish forest industry group Metsa-Serla Oy said in a statement on Wednesday it had signed a letter of intent with Swedish Industri Kapital on the sale of its chemicals operations for 1.05 billion markka.
"The sale of the chemicals business is in line with Metsa-Serla's strategy of focussing on its key business areas, which are printing papers and packaging materials," it said.

A Metsa-Serla official said by telephone the 1.05 billion markka price included "a significant gain on disposal" and the statement said the deal would strengthen the company's financial resources and equity ratio.
The official gave no further details.
"Metsa-Serla will have a 20 percent interest in the new company to be set up to continue (its) chemicals business, which it feels has considerable growth potential," Metsa-Serla added.
The chemicals business -- with plants in Finland, Sweden and the Netherlands -- currently has a turnover of 700 million markka and employs 350.
